audience.programmeDescription: The joint VU–UvA programme develops close reading and interpretation of Greek and Latin texts through language study, linguistics, literature, ancient history and philosophy. Students also examine how later societies interpreted antiquity and complete an independent classics thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers substantial related study in Greek archaeology, Athenian democracy, rhetoric and comparative mythology, including Ovid. VU builds from reading and translating Greek and Latin to interpreting original texts, studying how both languages changed, and conducting independent classics research. UCR’s related courses do not form that sustained sequence in classical texts and languages.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC curriculum includes 30 EC of elective study and a 12 EC thesis with a colloquium. Comedy is optional. The Dutch language test and any required remedial course carry no credits. Four specified courses require at least 85% attendance.

finding: Read all 25 component titles and values, notes on the electives and thesis, programme identity, no-match explanation, cohort label and limitation. Removed repeated source notes. The explanation gives concrete overlapping courses and describes the distinct source-language progression.
